inputs.title: The Thing
inputs.logline: On his first trip to the Learning Circle, Bo keeps packing and unpacking his conker because his tail might do “The Thing” — until Keen and Aida help him discover that the part he wants to hide may be the very thing new friends love first.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen tries to steal honey from under a sleeping Fuzzby, turning hunger into a tiptoe suspense game where every crunch and snore bubble threatens to expose him.
beats.want: Keen wants the honeycomb without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that wanting something does not make sneaking toward it brave or wise.
beats.kidRead: Sneaky steps, loud crunches, snore bubbles, and a sleeping bee on treasure.
beats.adultRead: A child’s appetite tries to outrun self-control while the world comically refuses to stay quiet.
beats.emotionalIntent: Playful tension; hold the audience in a giggly near-discovery state.

direction.premise: A small squirrel’s first-day worries become visible through a tail that poofs whenever the world feels too big, and the Crystal Bears help him move from hiding it to sharing it.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo walk into a new circle of friends while letting the thing he fears about himself be seen?
direction.theme: Belonging begins when the hidden part is witnessed kindly, not when it disappears.
direction.externalJourney: Bo leaves his hollow tree, walks the Whispering Woods path with Keen, meets Aida, reaches the Learning Circle, and joins the group through the playful discovery of his poofing tail.
direction.internalJourney: Bo moves from delay and self-protection to one small brave step, then to enough trust to let his tail become play instead of proof that he does not fit.
direction.relationshipChanges: Keen becomes Bo’s first safe peer by admiring what Bo is ashamed of; Aida becomes the elder who admits going forward can still feel hard; the Learning Circle shifts from imagined judging crowd to delighted friends; Fuzzby and Zenny close the episode by echoing the honeycomb game as a lighter aftertaste.
direction.emotionalCurve: Sneaky comic hunger opens the world, Aida’s vision turns attention toward Bo’s stuckness, Bo’s worry tightens through repetition, relief arrives through Keen’s admiration, honesty deepens on the forest log, confidence rises through the Crystal Calls, belonging blooms at the Learning Circle, and the ending releases into a gentle honeycomb callback.
direction.comedyCurve: Physical suspense and sneeze timing in Scene 1; conker packing repetition and tail poofs in Scene 3; command-performance poofs in Scene 4; Sunny’s over-bright welcome and the fluffy-firework tail in Scene 6; a final flower-disguise Fuzzby crash capped by Zenny’s tiny crack of amusement.
direction.setupPayoffMap: The honeycomb is set up as untouchable in Scene 1 and remains untouched in the final wide; Keen’s sneeze leads Aida to him and Bo; Bo’s repeated packing and conker handling show the loop he must break; the tail’s unwanted poof becomes first a private embarrassment, then a game, then a group delight; Aida’s “every single time” is paid off by Bo repeating it as he walks; Fuzzby’s “never ever” returns as Keen’s closing boundary.
direction.visualMotifs: The conker moving in and out of the satchel; Bo’s tail expanding and deflating; open door thresholds; paths curving forward; pink and blue light joining on the forest floor; honeycomb remaining just out of reach.
direction.sonicMotifs: Crunching stealth steps, snore-bubble pops, sneeze explosions, shave-and-a-haircut knock, tail POOF as soft comic firework, Aida’s bowl tone, rose-quartz G and aquamarine B joining under the path, Zenny’s quiet Ommmm bookend.
direction.climax: On the glowing forest path, after Aida and Keen make their Crystal Calls, Bo takes the first step, then another, choosing to go forward with his worry still present.
direction.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail becomes a source of play and connection, and later he sits with Keen drawing the new friends he was afraid to meet.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, giggly relief with a tiny ache left inside it: the honeycomb is still untouched, Bo’s worry mattered, and belonging did not require any part of him to vanish.

northStar.surfaceStory: At sunset in Keen’s garden, Fuzzby tries one last ridiculous flower disguise to reach the untouched honeycomb, crashes into Keen, gets the “Never, ever” boundary, and ends tangled in petals while Zenny quietly resumes meditation.
northStar.universalTruth: Sometimes the thing you want most is still not yours to take, and being loved does not mean every impulse gets a yes.
northStar.childClearWant: Fuzzby wants the honeycomb and is trying to sneak to it without being stopped.
northStar.emotionalNeed: Fuzzby needs to feel that a boundary is not banishment; he can crash, be corrected, and still belong in the garden’s little world.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If I make the plan grand enough and silly enough, the rule might not count for me.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Keen is the warm boundary: he does not shame Fuzzby, but he stops the behaviour. Zenny is the affectionate witness: her tiny escaped giggle tells us Fuzzby is still loved, not mocked or rejected.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: A child can be funny, persistent and adored — and still have to hear no.
northStar.sceneTurn: The flower disguise stops being clever the instant Fuzzby crashes into Keen’s back; the sneak game becomes a clear boundary callback.
audienceJourney: Recognise the honeycomb temptation from the opening.
Enjoy Fuzzby’s overcommitted disguise before it works even slightly.
Laugh at the body-first crash into Keen’s boundary.
Feel the rule land without the scene becoming stern.
Relax into Zenny’s tiny giggle and the calm final hold on the still-untouched honeycomb.
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: Warm comic closure with a small, satisfying firmness: the honeycomb remains untouched, Fuzzby remains included, and the garden is peaceful again.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any explanation of the lesson, apology, or reassurance. Keen’s body stopping the crash, Fuzzby’s dazed grass-level thumbs-up, Zenny’s one escaped smile, and the untouched honeycomb carry the meaning. Keep the locked dialogue verbatim only.
northStar.environmentPressure: The garden itself tempts and resists Fuzzby: flowers provide the absurd disguise, petals tangle him after the crash, low grass reduces him to a humbled thumbs-up, and the visible honeycomb keeps the desire present without rewarding it.

transformation.entryBelief: The honeycomb is still there, so one more magnificent plan might get around the rule.
transformation.entryFeeling: Buzzing with overconfident appetite and secret hope.
transformation.pressureBehaviour: He overcommits physically: disguises himself as a flower, sneaks too hard, flies with chaotic vertical overshoots, and lets momentum outrun judgement.
transformation.costlyChoice: After the crash and Keen’s boundary, he does not relaunch into another scheme; he stays down in the consequence long enough to offer the small dazed thumbs-up.
transformation.exitBelief: The rule is real even when he is funny, and being stopped does not mean he has been pushed out.
transformation.exitAction: He lies tangled in petals at grass level, processing “Ever?” while Zenny’s calm resumes and the honeycomb remains untouched.

tapestry.physicalMotif: The unreachable honeycomb and the failed flower disguise: want dressed up as innocence, then revealed by petals tangled around the would-be sneaker.
tapestry.sonicMotif: Fuzzby’s frantic buzz collapsing into crash and dazed “Bzzzzz,” answered by Zenny’s steady “Ommmm…”; chaos meets calm, then calm reclaims the garden.
tapestry.colourAndLightProgression: Warm sunset gold begins as temptation around the honeycomb, then softens into evening amber after the crash so the final image feels settled, not victorious.
tapestry.thematicVisualContrast: Fuzzby’s manic, erratic motion versus Keen’s grounded boundary and Zenny’s still meditation; impulse moves, care holds still.

treatments.name: 1. The Warm Boundary Holds Still
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience feels the scene as a giggly suspense release: Fuzzby’s final honey plan is ridiculous before it is dangerous, then the crash snaps the game into a clear, loving “no.” Kids laugh at the flower disguise, the thunk into Keen, and the petal tangle; adults feel the relief of a boundary delivered without rejection.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Keen’s steadiness governs the meaning. Fuzzby brings the want; Keen carries the necessary limit; Zenny confirms that the limit has not broken belonging. The emotional point of view is not “Fuzzby gets punished,” but “Fuzzby hits a boundary and the garden stays safe enough to laugh.”
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: movement against stillness. Fuzzby’s overcommitted, erratic flower-sneak keeps colliding with a world that does not join his fantasy: Keen gardening, Zenny meditating, the honeycomb untouched. Secondary mechanism: escalating overcommitment — the disguise is not subtle, so Fuzzby compensates by sneaking harder, which makes him less subtle.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby performs total belief in the disguise: chest proud inside the plan, flight too fast for stealth, vertical overshoots that keep betraying him, every correction creating a new wobble. The crash must be body-first, not line-first. After Keen’s “Never, ever – Fuzzby!” Fuzzby’s energy drains into confused processing: “Ever … Bzzzzz … Ever?” is a small dazed loop, not a debate. Keen is warm but immovable: he stops the behaviour with his whole grounded body before the line finishes. Zenny’s performance is almost entirely withheld — meditation, one tiny escaped smile and giggle, then a return to “Ommmm…” as affectionate punctuation.
treatments.visualGrammar: The frame treats stillness as moral clarity. Keen and Zenny are composed as anchored presences in the garden; Fuzzby is a streak of intention repeatedly failing to become stealth. The sunset gold remains tempting around the honeycomb, but after the crash the same light softens, making the boundary feel settled rather than stern. No lecture posture; the lesson is geometric: impulse travels, care holds.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera respects Keen’s grounded boundary and lets Fuzzby invade it. It does not safely wait for every gag; it allows Fuzzby to enter frames imperfectly, overshoot, and briefly outrun containment, but returns to Keen’s steadiness when the rule lands. With Zenny, the camera stays patient enough for her micro-reaction to become the punchline.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Fuzzby supplies almost all motion: bobbing, darting, overcorrecting, crashing, flopping. Keen’s movement is practical garden tending until the crash forces a firm stop. Zenny is a still point whose tiny facial release has value because the scene has rationed it. The contrast is the scene’s spine.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The honeycomb remains visible as desire in the scene’s depth whenever possible, not as a reward but as the unchanged fact. Garden stems, flowers and petals create layers that Fuzzby misuses as cover and then wears as consequence. Low grass at the end reduces him to the level of his mistake while Keen and Zenny’s calm continue around him.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Begin with calm evening routine. Let the suspicious flower-disguise rhythm interrupt the calm in small increasingly obvious pulses. Build to the crash as a sudden hard punctuation. After Keen’s boundary, drop the tempo sharply: Fuzzby’s dazed line has space, Zenny’s meditation reclaims the garden, then the one giggle releases the tension without undoing the rule.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by changed power and comic punctuation only: from temptation to attempted stealth, from stealth to impact, from impact to boundary, from boundary to Fuzzby processing, from processing to Zenny’s tiny release, then to the final held wide. No automatic reaction coverage; if the emotion has not changed, stay. If the rule has landed, cut cleanly before sentiment gathers.
treatments.openingImage: Sunset garden calm: the untouched honeycomb glows warmly in the distance while Keen tends the garden, and an obviously suspicious flower shape begins bobbing into the peaceful world as if it thinks it belongs there.
treatments.closingImage: A settled wide of the garden: the honeycomb still untouched, Zenny back in meditation, Keen’s boundary having held, and Fuzzby tangled low in petals — included in the peace, but not rewarded with the honey.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a flat garden two-shot with a bee gag pasted on top. The frame must argue: Fuzzby’s diagonal, unstable paths should visibly fail against Keen and Zenny’s calm verticals. I will resist any safe centered composition that lets the honeycomb disappear; the untouched object is the proof that the boundary worked.

treatments.name: 2. Fuzzby’s Magnificent Plan Collapses from the Inside
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience rides Fuzzby’s overconfidence first, so the crash is both surprise and comeuppance. Children feel like they are inside a silly secret mission; adults read the familiar logic of a child who believes costume plus effort might erase a rule. The emotional shift comes when the scene stops being a mission and becomes a soft landing after “no.”
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Fuzzby owns the subjective journey. The scene begins in his false belief — one more magnificent plan might work — and ends with him down in the grass, still loved, slowly understanding that “ever” means ever. Keen and Zenny are discovered by Fuzzby rather than presented as waiting judges.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: anticipation to reversal. The flower disguise promises clever infiltration; the body delivers blunt impact. Secondary mechanism: hiding failure — after the crash, the dazed thumbs-up tries to preserve dignity even while the petals tell the truth.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby is not sneaking quietly; he is performing the idea of sneaking at full Fuzzby intensity. His body keeps betraying the lie: altitude porpoises, little corrective bursts, wings working too hard, flower disguise lagging behind his intention. The instant of impact strips away the fantasy. Keen’s line is not angry volume; it is the surprised boundary of someone physically interrupted and immediately clear. Fuzzby’s “Ever … Bzzzzz … Ever?” is thought arriving in pieces. Zenny does not rescue him from embarrassment; her restrained giggle says he is seen and still welcome.
treatments.visualGrammar: The first half is subjective and slightly too grand for the actual scale of the plan: stems feel like corridors, petals like a heroic disguise, honey like a glowing destination. The crash breaks that fantasy into plain garden reality. Afterward, scale becomes humbling: grass blades, fallen petals, the unreachable honeycomb, and Zenny’s calm presence make Fuzzby’s plan feel small but not shaming.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera follows and struggles to keep up with Fuzzby’s attempted sneak, occasionally losing clean control because his body has no clean control. It can discover Keen late — the way Fuzzby does — so the audience shares the “oh no” instant of the boundary appearing too close. After the crash, the camera stops chasing and stays with the consequence long enough for the dazed processing to become funny and tender.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement begins as Fuzzby’s fantasy of mastery and becomes proof of his lack of control. Stillness arrives only after impact: Keen planted, Fuzzby grounded, Zenny’s meditation continuing. That stillness is not safe coverage; it is the emotional correction Fuzzby needed.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth is used like Fuzzby’s obstacle course. The honeycomb gleams ahead as the forbidden target; intervening flowers and garden shapes exaggerate the “mission” in his mind. Once he crashes, the same environment becomes evidence: petals tangled around him, grass around his face, honey still distant. The garden does not punish him; it simply refuses to collude.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Start with a stealth pulse that is already too fast. Let each adjustment intensify the absurdity: closer, higher, lower, almost concealed, not concealed at all. The crash is a rhythm break. Then slow everything down into the dazed “Ever” loop, followed by Zenny’s calm “Ommmm…” as the garden’s metronome returning.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Use fewer cuts during the approach so the audience feels the plan’s momentum as one doomed run. Cut sharply on the crash or immediately after it to mark the fantasy collapsing. After that, cuts must be sparse and thought-motivated: Fuzzby processing, Zenny noticing, Zenny releasing the tiny giggle, final wide. No cutting simply to show who is talking if the body already carries the line.
treatments.openingImage: From within or tight among Fuzzby’s flower disguise, the honeycomb shines ahead through petals like a forbidden prize, while his own bobbing motion makes the “clever” hiding place wobble suspiciously.
treatments.closingImage: The final wide recontextualizes his grand mission as tiny and finished: Fuzzby down among petals, Zenny calmly meditating again, and the honeycomb still exactly where it was — wanted, visible, not taken.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The risk is making the disguise readable but not experiential. I want the opening grammar to be seduced by Fuzzby’s plan, then embarrassed by reality. The camera should not politely frame the crash from a safe distance; it should be caught in his overcommitment and then have to recover into the truth of the space.

treatments.name: 3. The Garden Refuses to Help the Sneak
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience experiences the garden as a living comic partner. Every flower, petal and grass blade seems to know the honeycomb is off-limits and quietly exposes Fuzzby’s plan. Children enjoy the environment joining the joke; adults feel the ordinary truth that boundaries are easier when the whole little world supports them.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The point of view belongs to the garden’s calm order. Keen tends it, Zenny harmonizes with it through meditation, and Fuzzby tries to misuse it as camouflage. The emotional meaning is that belonging to the garden does not mean bending the garden’s rules around your want.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary mechanism: environmental participation. Flowers provide the disguise, then betray it; petals become the costume and then the tangle; grass turns the aftermath into a humbled little stage. Secondary mechanism: concealment to revelation — the “flower” is funny because it is trying to pass as innocent until motion reveals the appetite inside it.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby treats the garden as his accomplice and is offended when physics disagrees. His flight remains manic and vertically erratic even while pretending to be a flower; the more the environment catches on him, the more he commits. Keen’s gardening is attentive and unshowy, making him part of the garden’s order before he becomes the boundary. Zenny’s meditation is not indifference; it is trust in the calm she is holding. Her tiny smile and giggle must feel like a leak in the stillness, then she reseals it with “Ommmm…”

treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience rides inside Fuzzby’s ridiculous certainty that one last disguise can make the rule disappear, then laughs and exhales when the garden, Keen, and Zenny let the boundary hold without pushing him out.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Treatment 2 is the spine because it gives the scene a live dramatic question: will Fuzzby’s grand little self-deception carry him to the honey, or will reality catch up first? Its subjective approach makes the crash more than slapstick — it is the exact instant his fantasy collapses into a loving no. That is the strongest Crystal Bears shape: child-readable mission comedy with adult-readable boundary truth. Treatment 3 should be folded in as the environmental grammar: petals, stems, grass, depth, and the untouched honeycomb must actively expose the want without becoming magical or busy. Treatment 1 supplies the emotional landing: Keen’s grounded warmth, Zenny’s tiny withheld release, and the final wide where Fuzzby remains included but unrewarded. The combined treatment gives us the cleanest meaning: Fuzzby is not bad for wanting; he is safe enough to be stopped. It also gives the most memorable visual idea — a flower disguise that thinks it is heroic, while the whole garden quietly reveals it is not.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: No treatment is selected as a flat standalone. Treatment 1 alone risks making the scene too externally governed by Keen’s steadiness and could drift into safe anchored compositions if handled literally; we keep its boundary warmth but reject any fixed-position staging or polite two-shot logic. Treatment 3 alone risks letting the garden’s comic agency dilute the relationship heart or feel like the environment is ‘teaching’ Fuzzby; we keep its occlusion, drag, sway, and depth but reject anything magical, decorative, or generic. Treatment 2 is accepted as the primary engine because it does not depend on fixed character lanes, keeping everyone visible, habitual action/reaction coverage, repeated close-up punctuation, safe camera placement, mechanical shot counts, or merely illustrating the script. The camera must be caught in Fuzzby’s overcommitment, discover Keen’s boundary experientially, and recover into the settled truth of the garden. Cuts are only for changed power, comic reversal, or emotional settling — never automatic coverage.

FUZZBY sneaks through the grass wearing a FLOWER DISGUISE — petals around his head like he's trying to blend in. He freezes, pretending to be a flower. Nothing happens. He peeks around. Creeps toward the honey. A twig SNAPs.
He freezes. Moves again … Trips into a BUZZ-CRASH AND TUMBLES HEAD OVER HEELS TOWRDS KEEN. He face-plants into Keen's back. Keen does not turn around. He simply raises one paw.

direction.premise: A small squirrel’s first-day worries become visible through a tail that poofs whenever the world feels too big, and the Crystal Bears help him move from hiding it to sharing it.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo walk into a new circle of friends while letting the thing he fears about himself be seen?
direction.theme: Belonging begins when the hidden part is witnessed kindly, not when it disappears.
direction.externalJourney: Bo leaves his hollow tree, walks the Whispering Woods path with Keen, meets Aida, reaches the Learning Circle, and joins the group through the playful discovery of his poofing tail.
direction.internalJourney: Bo moves from delay and self-protection to one small brave step, then to enough trust to let his tail become play instead of proof that he does not fit.
direction.relationshipChanges: Keen becomes Bo’s first safe peer by admiring what Bo is ashamed of; Aida becomes the elder who admits going forward can still feel hard; the Learning Circle shifts from imagined judging crowd to delighted friends; Fuzzby and Zenny close the episode by echoing the honeycomb game as a lighter aftertaste.
direction.emotionalCurve: Sneaky comic hunger opens the world, Aida’s vision turns attention toward Bo’s stuckness, Bo’s worry tightens through repetition, relief arrives through Keen’s admiration, honesty deepens on the forest log, confidence rises through the Crystal Calls, belonging blooms at the Learning Circle, and the ending releases into a gentle honeycomb callback.

direction.visualMotifs: The conker moving in and out of the satchel; Bo’s tail expanding and deflating; open door thresholds; paths curving forward; pink and blue light joining on the forest floor; honeycomb remaining just out of reach.

direction.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail becomes a source of play and connection, and later he sits with Keen drawing the new friends he was afraid to meet.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, giggly relief with a tiny ache left inside it: the honeycomb is still untouched, Bo’s worry mattered, and belonging did not require any part of him to vanish.

performances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, tangled and stunned at Keen’s side after the impact.
performances.emotionalEntry: Absorbs the thunk with patient focus; not angry, just instantly certain.
performances.emotionalExit: Still, protective, boundary held; leaves no room for another attempt.
performances.pace: Slow and settled after the fast impact; let the sudden calm be the comedy.
performances.rhythm: Three grounded beats: Never / ever / Fuzzby. The dash is a controlled catch, not melodrama.
performances.pauses: Let the paw rise and hold before the first word. Tiny weight on the dash before naming him.

performances.expectedTiming: Start only after the body-first thunk has compressed and Keen’s paw is already lifted; line should sit in the abrupt stillness.

performances.voiceIdentity: Fuzzby: buoyant show-off energy drained down to a tiny, buzzy survivor wobble.
performances.dramaticIntention: Check whether Keen’s rule is truly absolute while trying to keep one crumb of dignity.
performances.subtext: I may have lost, but I would like credit for technically still participating.
performances.relationshipTarget: Keen first, then a sideways hope that Zenny noticed the heroic thumbs-up.
performances.emotionalEntry: Knocked-low, delayed processing; brain and buzz are restarting at different speeds.
performances.emotionalExit: Confused acceptance with a small self-awarding thumbs-up.
performances.pace: Very slow and dazed; each piece arrives after the previous one has failed to become a thought.
performances.rhythm: Fragmented loop: question fragment, faulty buzz, question fragment. Let the second 'Ever?' be smaller and more hopeful.
performances.pauses: The ellipses are stunned processing gaps, not theatrical suspense. Hold them just long enough to feel the delayed flop.
performances.breaths: Weak little inhale before the first word; the buzz should leak out like leftover motor, not a fresh gag.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Keep him low in the grass. The tiny thumbs-up should feel like it costs almost all his remaining energy.

performances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice follows the body’s loss of power: mouth, buzz, and thought all wobble through the same dazed loop.
performances.expectedTiming: Begin after a low stunned pause. Let the flop land before the final hopeful 'Ever?' if editorial timing allows.

performances.speaker: Zenny
performances.voiceIdentity: Zenny: compact, centered, minimal; comedy comes from how little she gives away.
performances.dramaticIntention: Restore calm to herself and the garden while refusing to reward the chaos too much.
performances.subtext: I am not reacting. I am absolutely noticing.
performances.relationshipTarget: Mostly inward meditation, with a tiny awareness of Fuzzby in the grass.
performances.emotionalEntry: Stillness re-forming after the tumble; she is choosing calm before curiosity wins.
performances.emotionalExit: Calm surface maintained, but a smile is about to escape.
performances.pace: Unhurried, soft, even; no performative mysticism.
performances.rhythm: One smooth sustained note with the faintest living warmth inside it.
performances.pauses: Hold Zenny’s stillness before the line; the ellipsis lets the hum dissolve into the moment she opens her eyes.
performances.breaths: Silent, settled inhale before the hum; no gasp.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Her body remains compact on the leaf. The line should not anticipate the giggle yet; it is the calm before the leak.

performances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice supports her almost-motionless body; the humour is restraint, not reaction.
performances.expectedTiming: Delay until calm has visibly resumed. Hold the hum under her stillness before the eye-open beat.

performances.dramaticIntention: Tuck the escaped giggle back into calm and let the garden end untouched.
performances.subtext: You are ridiculous, and everything is okay.
performances.relationshipTarget: Herself and the garden calm; Fuzzby only receives a tiny trace of fondness.
performances.emotionalEntry: A small smile and giggle have just slipped out.

orderedEvents.text: Keen tends to his garden. Golden sunset. The honeycomb still sits untouched.

FUZZBY sneaks through the grass wearing a FLOWER DISGUISE — petals around his head like he's trying to blend in. He freezes, pretending to be a flower. Nothing happens. He peeks around. Creeps toward the honey. A twig SNAPs.
He freezes. Moves again … Trips into a BUZZ-CRASH AND TUMBLES HEAD OVER HEELS TOWRDS KEEN. He face-plants into Keen's back. Keen does not turn around. He simply raises one paw.

showrunnerJudgement: Pass. I tried to break it on the usual Crystal Bears failure points — safe coverage, reaction-shot ping-pong, stern lesson posture, decorative Zenny business, and losing the honeycomb as the visible proof of the rule — but the scene’s accumulated behaviour holds. Fuzzby’s want is clear, Keen’s boundary is bodily and warm, Zenny’s tiny release confirms belonging, and the untouched honeycomb remains the emotional argument rather than a prop. The crash and boundary would still read muted through silhouette and staging: motion invades, care holds still, impulse is stopped without exile.
treatmentComparison: The storyboard substantially preserves the selected treatment’s central experience: giggly suspense release moving into a loving no. The opening frame keeps sunset calm, Keen’s gardening, and the honeycomb in depth before Fuzzby invades as the obviously wrong flower. The comic mechanism remains movement against stillness rather than a generic chase. The turn lands where it should — the disguise stops being a game when Fuzzby crashes into Keen — and the aftermath drops tempo instead of escalating into more business. Zenny is rationed correctly: meditation, almost-withheld amusement, then return to calm. The closing image keeps the garden peaceful, the honeycomb untouched, and Fuzzby included at grass level, so the boundary feels settled rather than punitive.
packingJudgement: Packing passes. The two-unit split is not an avoidable join under the 30-second rule: S8.SH1 plus S8.SH2 totals 34 seconds, and the split sits on a real dramatic boundary between impact/boundary and low-grass processing. Compressing the stealth escalation, crash, firm callback, dazed loop, Zenny release, and final wide into one 30-second request would likely flatten the earned tempo drop. S8.SH2 is short but has one coherent job — aftermath and re-settling — and it keeps the quiet beats together rather than fragmenting them into reaction coverage.
